latin: Qui crediderit intentionem dici de omni esse aliam ab ea quam dixit praecedens conclusio defendere non potest Aristotelem a Theophrasto, quod ex maiori necessaria et minori inuenta sequatur conclusio necessaria.
translation: Whoever believes that the sense of 'predicated of all' is other than what the preceding conclusion stated cannot defend Aristotle against Theophrastus, that a necessary conclusion follows from a necessary major premise and a minor premise that is merely found true.
translation_note: Refers to the ancient dispute, reported for Theophrastus, over whether a necessary conclusion can follow a syllogism with an assertoric (non-modal) minor premise (farmer1998:13876).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-light-batch2, from Latin at farmer1998:13876
not_established: No secondary scholarship discussing thesis 9.6 specifically was found in the corpus harvest; the attribution to al-Farabi rests on the 900 Conclusions' own section rubric, not on external confirmation.
